cards.card_text: Some time later, two officers offend their master, Pharaoh, the king of Egypt: his chief cupbearer and his chief baker.
cards.verse_text: Some time later, the king’s cupbearer and baker offended their master, the king of Egypt.
cards.snippet: Some time later, the king’s cupbearer and baker offended their master, the king of Egypt.

cards.card_text: Now Elihu paints a picture, baker: suppose someone tells God he has endured his punishment and will offend no more.
cards.verse_text: Suppose someone says to God, ‘I have endured my punishment; I will offend no more.
cards.snippet: Suppose someone says to God, ‘I have endured my punishment; I will offend no more.

cards.card_text: Then the proverb puts an offended brother right next to a fortified city, side by side, like they're standing in a lineup.
cards.verse_text: An offended brother is harder to win than a fortified city, and disputes are like the bars of a castle.
